lines.note: Namakabe is a freshly made wall or earthen wall, still not set or dried. The right edge shows no secure period after freſca; none is supplied merely because this is a complete entry.
Namako, with the synonym tawarago, is described literally as sea slugs. This is the historical dictionary's comparison for the edible sea animal, not a modern zoological classification.
Completes the account by saying that these sea animals are eaten raw in Japan. Cruas agrees with the Portuguese leſmas on the preceding row.

Namachi and namagi are alternatives for fresh blood; lowercase l introduces the alternative. The faint mark after Namachi is not secure enough to add punctuation against the aligned draft; the second form retains its lowercase initial.
Namadaikon is raw radish, glossed in the plural as raw radishes. The Portuguese Rabãos retains its historical spelling and the tilde over a.
Namadara denotes a fresh fish compared with hake in the Portuguese gloss. Freſco refers to the fish's fresh state; the definition is not a claim of exact species equivalence.

runs.text: Ferro brando na tempera, como o

lines.note: Namagane is iron that is soft in its temper, illustrated by sword metal below. The final o resumes ferro and is not the beginning of another entry.
Completes the comparison with the metal of katanas. Catanas occurs inside the Portuguese explanation and is printed in the same italic style here.
Namagatten is incomplete or inadequate understanding. The double t is visible and is not reduced to match an imagined simpler form.
Namagatsuo is described as a certain fish compared with shad-like fish. The doubled uu sequence is retained in the historical spelling, and Hũ is not expanded to hum.
Namagokoro is paraphrased as an imperfect or half-hearted intention. Namaxij cocorozaxi is a Japanese synonym phrase after i, not a term embedded within Portuguese prose; Võ- begins vontade.
Completes vontade and describes imperfect, slight affection or intention. The adjective leue qualifies the weakness of that feeling rather than physical weight.
Namagokorona describes a person with little affection or commitment. The final na marks the adjectival expression, while the following row adds another aspect of the gloss.
Adds 'or little knowledge' to the description of the person. The short continuation is kept separately rather than merged into the preceding physical row.
Namagome is raw rice. The grave over the Portuguese u is visible and remains crù rather than being silently modernized to cru.

runs.text: Couſa que corta mal, como Cata-

lines.note: Namagire is something that cuts poorly, first illustrated by a katana. The Japanese sword term is physically divided Cata- / na and remains inside the Portuguese explanation.

runs.text: na, &c. ¶ Item, per met. Peßoa que

lines.note: Completes Catana and introduces a metaphorical use for a person. Per met. explicitly shifts from a poorly cutting blade to the indecision described below.

runs.text: não ſe reſolue de todo em dar reposta, ou em

lines.note: Describes someone who cannot fully resolve to give an answer. The historical reposta is retained without inserting the s of modern resposta; the alternative action follows below.
Completes the metaphor with inability to settle on doing something. This closes the same indecisiveness definition rather than introducing a general verb phrase.
Namagireni is the corresponding adverb, labeled Adu. The close sequence guire is legible and remains distinct from the following guri in 'chestnuts'.
Namaguri means raw chestnuts. The shift from guire to guri is meaningful and agrees with the entirely different Portuguese gloss.

runs.text: Couſa que fede a crua, como pei-

lines.note: Namagusai describes a raw or fishy smell. The example pei- continues as peixe, explaining the odor rather than introducing a further namagu- form.
Completes peixe and names namasu as another example of something with that raw smell. Namaſu is embedded in Portuguese prose and is visibly italic here; it also has its own entry in column 2.
Namajij is glossed here as raw Japanese acorns. This food entry must not be interpreted through the following, differently glossed namajijna merely because their spellings overlap.

runs.text: Couſa, que não deuera ſer, ou mal

lines.note: Namajijna describes something that ought not to be, or is ill employed. The Portuguese begins a judgment of ill-advised or unsuitable action, not a definition of raw acorns.

runs.text: empregada por não ſoceder bem, ou não con-

lines.note: Explains that the thing is ill employed because it does not turn out well or is unsuitable. The historical ſoceder is preserved, with con- continuing into conuir below.
Completes conuir, 'to be fitting or suitable'. The brief continuation belongs to the preceding Portuguese verb and is not a Japanese form.
The adverb is printed Namajiini, with two i letters after j, correcting the missing i in OCR Namajini. The supplied NINJAL Namajiini entry independently supports the lexical form.

runs.text: Sal crù. i, Aßi como ſae da mari-

lines.note: Namajiuô denotes raw or unrefined salt as it leaves the saltworks. The visible circumflex over final o is retained even though the supplied lexical index gives unaccented Namajiuo; mari- continues below.

runs.text: nha ſem ſe tornar acozer, nem purificar.

lines.note: Completes marinha and explains that the salt has not been boiled again or purified. The close printed acozer is retained rather than introducing a modernizing word break.
Namaita is a green, unseasoned board. The example starts a comparison with driving a nail into such a board; cu- is the beginning of cugui, completed on the next row.
Completes the comparison: speaking as one drives a nail into a green board. The Portuguese cou continues into couſas without a printed terminal hyphen; the Japanese is a standalone example.

runs.text: ſas demaneira que fiquem bem entendidas, ou

lines.note: Completes couſas and says that the speech leaves matters clearly understood. The source's close demaneira is preserved, while the comparison continues toward the board securely nailed in place.

runs.text: arrecadadas como a taboa verde bem pregada.

lines.note: The metaphor presents the matters as securely lodged or settled, like the well-nailed green board. Arrecadadas belongs to the preceding couſas, not to the board itself.

Namameku is to be graceful and attractive in appearance. The abbreviated principal forms u and eita belong to this verb, and the existing vistoſo s/t reading is retained without global reclassification.

runs.text: nas feiçoẽs, & meneos: commummẽte ſe diz

lines.note: Specifies facial features and movements or bearing, then notes customary usage. The historical feiçoẽs and abbreviated commummẽte are preserved rather than expanded or respelled.
Completes the usage note: the expression is commonly applied to women. This reports the dictionary's scope of usage rather than imposing a general modern restriction.
Namana is an adjectival expression for something raw. Its na is retained within the printed headword, not separated according to modern grammatical analysis.
Namanamashii describes something raw or green. The following two indented forms are derivatives of this adjective, not continuations of the Portuguese gloss.
Namanamashisa is the corresponding quality noun in -sa. Its subordinate indentation and long ſ are preserved; no unprinted Portuguese explanation is added to the transcription.
Namanamashuu is the contracted adverbial form. The scan shows a single final u with a caron, followed by a period; the OCR's extra terminal i is part of its misreading of that u.
Namanarina describes something not fully completed or perfected. The following sushi example begins with the adjective divided after Na-.

Completes namanarina sushi and describes fish prepared by a certain preserving process. The Japanese phrase is an example, so its individual words are not marked as terms embedded in Portuguese prose.
The preserving process is still incomplete. The feminine imperfeita refers back to conſerua; the existing italic s/t transcription in està is retained.
Namanurui denotes something very lukewarm or cool. The following example extends the physical lack of heat to an action lacking energy.
Namanurui koto illustrates a tepid or half-hearted undertaking. The Portuguese fei- continues as feita and is not part of the Japanese expression.
Completes the metaphor as something done with little diligence. This closes the example before the separately listed adverb.

Namanuruu is the adverb corresponding to namanurui. The damaged consonant before final ǔ is read r, correcting OCR Namanuiǔ; the surviving shoulder and the supplied NINJAL Namanurǔ entry support this choice.

Namakeru is introduced as a new verb, with principal forms uru and eta. The dictionary groups softness and effeminacy with negligence in its historical gloss; the flush-left entry is not a continuation from column 1.
Completes the verb's gloss with being negligent or slovenly. This short italic row belongs to namaqe and is retained independently as a physical continuation.

Namakemono is alternatively paraphrased as namaketa hito, a person characterized by that behavior. A faint mark after the headword is not secure enough to add a period against the aligned draft; the lowercase l remains the alternative marker.
Completes the dictionary's description as soft, effeminate, and of little practical use. The scan's crossed f in efeminado corrects OCR eſeminado and agrees with the same word in the verb entry.

runs.text: Pao, ou lenha que ainda està verde.

lines.note: Namaki is wood or firewood that is still green or unseasoned. Pao is the Portuguese wood term here, not bread; no unprinted nasal mark is added.
Namari is the metal lead. The next entry repeats the written stem but supplies verbal inflections and different meanings, so the two records remain distinct.
Namaru is first explained as not pronouncing words correctly. The inflectional atta is printed with two t letters and belongs to this verb, unlike the preceding metal noun.

runs.text: palauras, nem cõ ſeus acentos, &c. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Completes the reference to words and their accents. The scan clearly includes final s in palauras, correcting singular OCR palaura; Itẽ introduces a separate sense below.

runs.text: Estar a eſpada, ou Catana deſtemperada, co-

lines.note: A further sense concerns a sword or katana losing its proper temper. Catana is a Japanese sword term within the Portuguese explanation; the printed s/t forms are not globally regularized.

runs.text: mo depois de cortar algũa couſa quente, &c.

lines.note: Completes the comparison with a blade after cutting something hot. This reports the historical dictionary's illustrative explanation and does not add a modern metallurgical claim.
Namasaba is glossed as fresh sauelha, using the dictionary's Portuguese fish comparison. The long ſ in the Japanese headword remains distinct from the capital S beginning the gloss.

runs.text: Certa iguaria de peixe crù com outras

lines.note: Namasu is a prepared dish of raw fish with other ingredients. This explains the food named earlier inside the namagusai gloss; the Portuguese crù has a grave accent.
Completes the ingredients as mixtures of herbs and similar additions. Misturas retains the aligned draft's s/t reading; the surrounding text does not license a blanket long-s substitution.

runs.text: Paßaro morto que eſtà ainda freſco.

lines.note: Namatori is explicitly a dead bird that is still fresh. The definition concerns freshness after death, not a live bird; the doubled-s ligature in Paßaro is preserved.
Namashii is glossed as something raw. The scan shows u with a grave in crùa, correcting OCR cria while retaining the unusual accent rather than silently writing modern crua.

runs.text: Couſa que não deuera ſer, ou que

lines.note: Namashiina denotes something that ought not to be or is inappropriate. This judgment differs from the preceding rawness gloss and continues through the following Portuguese row.
Completes the adjective's explanation as something that does not fit or suit the occasion. The joined apropoſito is preserved here, unlike the visibly separated a propoſito in the next entry.

This entire physical row was omitted by the OCR candidate. The scan supplies the adverb Namaxijni and introduces a way of characterizing something as ill employed or inappropriate; its complete new crop preserves both the headword and the right-edge algũa.

runs.text: couſa mal empregada, ou que não diz, nem vẽ

lines.note: Continues the restored Namaxijni definition: an expression for something ill employed or unsuitable. The abbreviated vẽ remains unexpanded and leads into its contextual qualification below.

runs.text: a propoſito do tempo, ou de outra circunſtancia.

lines.note: Specifies unsuitability to the time or another circumstance. This row belongs to the newly restored adverb entry, not directly to the earlier adjective.
Begins an example contrasting large stature with a lack of usefulness or competence. The printed vô- and final iccô have circumflexes, while the following row supplies a differently marked word.
Completes the contrast by calling the person inept or unserviceable. Buchôfǒna visibly combines a circumflex and a caron; Quanto à starts the Portuguese qualification 'as regards'.

runs.text: eſtatura grãde he, mas deſconueniente, porq̃he

lines.note: Says that the person is large in stature, but disadvantageously so. The tilde abbreviations grãde and porq̃he are preserved, and the reason follows on the next row.
Explains the criticism as being very negligent and of little use. A new example begins Nama- at the right edge, not another headword.

runs.text: xijno cotouo iuǒ yorimo mugon iraita.

lines.note: The example contrasts saying something inappropriate with keeping silent, as the Portuguese translation confirms. The historical form iraita is retained; no modernizing substitution is made from the translation alone.

runs.text: Milhor foy calar que dizer couſa fora de pro-

lines.note: Translates the preference as it being better to remain silent than to say something out of place. The historical Milhor and foy are retained, and pro- continues into propoſito.
Completes 'out of place, and not fitting'. The printed quadraſe has one long-s type, which is not doubled to match modern quadrasse.
Namayaki and namayakina describe something badly or insufficiently roasted. The lowercase l introduces the alternative form, and the double-s ligature of aßada is preserved.
Namayakini is the associated adverb. Its final ni contrasts with the preceding attributive na and remains a separate short entry.

runs.text: Pano, ou mela que ſe gèra no roſto,

lines.note: This namazzu denotes a patch or discoloration of the skin. The Portuguese reads Pano, correcting OCR Pino; the context and surviving a support that choice, distinct from the fish entry below.
Adds that the discoloration can occur elsewhere on the body, then gives an example meaning that such a patch forms. The double zz is retained in the Japanese example.
Translates the appearance of the patch or spot. The existing s/t reading in esta is left unchanged rather than converted solely because nearby isolated s letters are long.
A separate homographic entry defines namazzu as a river fish. It must not be merged with the preceding skin-discoloration sense merely because the headwords are identical.

runs.text: Liſonjas de peßoa que não he

lines.note: Namazzuishoo denotes the flattery of someone not yet skilled at flattering. The damaged vowel is read o in peßoa rather than OCR peßea; the scan also shows two separated baseline dots after the headword; both are retained, with the extra dot treated as probable printed punctuation.
Completes the definition as flattery by someone not yet adept at it. The example starts the same term divided at Namazzui-, and the aligned destra s/t reading is retained.

runs.text: Dizer liſonjas que logo ſe enten-

lines.note: The example means uttering flattery that is immediately recognized as such. The ô of the divided noun is a circumflex, while yǔ has a caron.
Completes the explanation that the compliments are recognized for what they are. Entendem is physically divided across the preceding hyphen and this row.
Namazukenai describes laziness and negligence. The historical Portuguese Priguiçoſo is retained rather than modernized, and the two following indented forms derive from this adjective.
Namazukenasa is the corresponding quality noun in -sa. The line has no Portuguese gloss, and its subordinate indentation is retained without adding text to the transcription.
Namazukenoo is the contracted adverbial form. The final o has a downward-pointing caron; no unprinted i or u is supplied after it.
Namazuki is the act of inadequately pounding rice. Pilar is the verb for pounding in this gloss, not the noun meaning a column or support.
Namazukina describes rice that has been poorly pounded. The final na supplies the attributive form related to the preceding action noun.
Namazukini is the associated adverb in ni. Its short grammatical label remains italic and is not incorporated into the Japanese word.
Nameru is glossed as lightly tasting or sampling. The physical division leuemen- / te is retained, and the principal forms belong to the new verb entry.
Completes 'lightly', gives sweet things and salt as examples, and starts canrouo namuru. The final na- continues the verb on the next row and is not part of the Portuguese list.

runs.text: Gostar com a boca doçura, ou ſuaui-

lines.note: Completes namuru and begins the translation as tasting sweetness or heavenly delight with the mouth. The right edge reads ſuaui- with a hyphen, correcting OCR ſuauis.; it joins dade below.
Completes ſuauidade do ceo, 'sweetness or delight of heaven'. This is the last body row; the separately placed Name. below is a catchword, not another instance of this definition.
